text: A test that only calls your function correctly, once, with valid input, proves almost nothing. Most real-world smart contract exploits happened on code paths nobody wrote a test for.
Here's a typical happy-path test: deposit a clean amount, withdraw it, check the balance. It's not wrong — it just proves the function works once, called correctly, by someone not trying to break it.

A rigorous test asserts the opposite: withdrawing more than the balance reverts with the right error, and an unauthorized caller can't reach a privileged function. expectRevert and prank are built exactly for this.
Rigorous coverage means five categories: the happy path, boundary values, every revert condition firing, access control holding, and state staying correct across call sequences.
The happy path is the easy ten percent. Lesson 2 automates the rest — fuzz testing throws thousands of boundary values at a function automatically.
